title: Khoa Tran Engineering Portfolio
description: Case studies, system design notes, and interactive engineering experiments.

items.title: HyperLogLog and the Question Bloom Filters Can't Answer
items.summary: Run a real HyperLogLog sketch — measure its estimation error against a true count and the theoretical standard error, watch the small-range correction matter, then merge two overlapping sketches for a real union estimate.

items.title: LSM Trees and the Write You'll Pay for Later
items.summary: Run a real log-structured merge tree — measure read amplification growing unbounded without compaction, then measure the real write-amplification cost of bounding it.

items.title: Raft and the Commit Rule Replica Count Alone Can't Prove
items.summary: Run Raft's real election restriction and commit-index safety rule — see why a stale node can't win an election no matter how many peers are alive, and why a majority of replicas alone still can't prove a log entry is safely committed.

items.title: Two-Phase Commit vs. Saga: What Atomicity Actually Costs
items.summary: Run the real 2PC blocking failure and the real Saga compensation-failure gap on the same kind of transaction — see exactly what atomicity costs, and exactly what giving it up costs instead.

items.title: Bloom Filters and the Capacity You Can't See Coming
items.summary: Run a real bit-array Bloom filter — measure its false-positive rate against the closed-form formula, then overload it past design capacity and watch the rate climb for real, not just in a formula.

items.title: Consistent Hashing and the Rebalancing Nobody Notices
items.summary: Run the real hash-ring placement algorithm against naive modulo hashing on the same key set — see how little of the keyspace a ring actually moves when a node joins or leaves, and what happens without enough virtual nodes to spread the luck around.

items.title: CRDTs: What to Do Once You Know Two Writes Are Concurrent
items.summary: Run a real G-Counter against a naive LWW register, and a real OR-Set against a naive 2P-Set — see exactly which concurrent updates the naive designs silently lose, and why detecting concurrency is only half the problem.

items.title: Merkle Trees and the Diff Nobody Has to Compute
items.summary: Run a real Merkle-tree targeted diff against a naive full scan on the same two datasets — see the O(1) proof of full equality, the near-O(log n) cost of a sparse diff, and the honest case where the targeted walk actually loses.

items.title: Vector Clocks and the Clock Skew That Fools Last-Write-Wins
items.summary: Run the real happens-before/happens-after/concurrent test on a scripted causal history, then watch a naive last-write-wins resolver flip its answer under clock skew alone — while the causal verdict never moves.

items.title: Backpressure: Four Policies, One Overload
items.summary: Block, drop-new, drop-old, and circuit breaker, run against the same producer that outruns its consumer — including proof that drop-new and drop-old discard the same number of items, but never the same ones.

items.title: Cache Freshness: What Stale-While-Revalidate Actually Buys You
items.summary: Three real cache-freshness policies run against the same origin outage — TTL-blocking errors, stale-while-revalidate never blocks at all, and stale-if-error sits in between, paying for a synchronous origin attempt even when it ends up serving the same stale content SWR would have served for free.

items.title: Canary Deploys and the Sample Size Nobody Checks
items.summary: A real two-proportion z-test canary analysis, run stage by stage — proving that the same real regression can go completely undetected at a small sample size and get caught at a larger one, using the exact statistic, not a story about it.

items.title: Distributed Locks: Redlock and the Pause That Breaks It
items.summary: Run the real Redlock quorum algorithm against nodes you crash yourself, then simulate the exact pause Martin Kleppmann's 2016 critique is about — and see why Antirez's own rebuttal doesn't actually disagree with it.

items.title: gRPC vs REST: When the Smaller Payload Loses
items.summary: A real harness measuring gRPC against REST for the same data, same server, same Go process — and REST wins throughput at every concurrency level tested for a small payload, and at half the concurrency levels tested for a 100x larger one.

items.title: Leader Election: Running the Actual Bully Algorithm, Not a Diagram of It
items.summary: Crash the leader and watch the real Bully algorithm elect a new one, message by message — including the O(n^2) worst case the protocol is criticized for.

items.title: Connection Pooling: When PgBouncer Actually Helps
items.summary: A real harness measuring PgBouncer against direct Postgres across two connection lifecycles — the advantage widens under one and reverses under the other, so 'add a pooler' isn't a universal answer.

items.title: Field Note: What My Own Git Log Proves About Spec-Driven Development
items.summary: PFM's governance docs claim every business rule traces from spec to test to code. A plain git log, not the docs, is what actually proves it — and it also shows two honest cases of deliberately not fixing something.

items.title: The Hidden Costs of Firebase Cloud Functions
items.summary: A follow-up to the field note on choosing Firebase Functions over Cloud Run: two costs the concurrency model doesn't advertise on its own.

items.title: ADR: Tracing vs Metrics for Observability in Aegis
items.summary: An Architecture Decision Record on why distributed tracing and metrics answer different questions in Aegis, and which one should gate a page for what.

items.title: Database Indexing for Time-Series: B-Tree vs BRIN in PostgreSQL
items.summary: Why a Block Range Index, not the default B-Tree, is the right structure for naturally time-ordered data — and why QuantAlpha's tick-ingestion pipeline hasn't needed it yet.

items.title: Gossip Protocol Visualizer: How Cluster Membership Actually Spreads
items.summary: A real push-based epidemic broadcast, run and scrubbed round by round, showing why gossip converges in O(log n) rounds instead of O(n).

items.title: Rate Limiting Algorithms: Token Bucket vs Leaky Bucket vs Fixed Window
items.summary: Three rate limiting algorithms, run for real against the same burst scenario, to show what each one actually does differently — not just what it's named.

items.title: WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events: What Holding 5,000 Connections Open Actually Costs
items.summary: A real harness measuring server memory for thousands of concurrent WebSocket vs SSE connections — written before the article, per the lesson from three prior benchmark rewrites.

items.title: Designing a Global API Gateway: Edge Routing Beyond a Single Aegis Instance
items.summary: Aegis's GraphQL gateway solves API shape for one instance. This is the layer above it a real deployment would need once there's more than one — and why that's a different problem, not a bigger version of the same one.

items.title: The SPA Google Never Saw
items.summary: This portfolio was a client-rendered SPA on GitHub Pages for months. Every deep link a crawler could find returned 404. Here's how I found it, and what I built instead of migrating frameworks.

items.title: ADR: Why Prerender Instead of Migrating to Next.js
items.summary: This portfolio's original decision to build a custom JAMstack instead of using Next.js still held once a crawler-visibility bug surfaced. Here's why the fix was a build step, not a framework migration.

items.title: Field Note: A Diagram That Wouldn't Render
items.summary: A sequence diagram in a new case study failed to parse. The cause wasn't the character I suspected first — and the fix I tried second broke the same way for a different reason.

items.title: Field Note: Measuring Contrast Instead of Guessing at It
items.summary: A prior audit flagged 44 text-slate-400 occurrences as 'potentially borderline' and correctly refused to fix them blind. Building a real contrast checker turned that judgment call into a number — and found two unrelated bugs on the way.

items.title: PFM: A Spec-Driven, Invite-Only Personal Finance Tracker
items.summary: A React 19 + Go financial tracker built spec-first: every business rule traces from an SRS to an SDS to a passing integration test, with a hard server-side boundary between the browser and the API.

items.title: Building Jujuja: A Production Quest System for Burst Traffic
items.summary: How we built the Jujuja backend to handle 1,500 concurrent users per minute during campaign bursts, processing daily quests and loyalty points using BullMQ and NestJS.

items.title: Designing a Multi-Role HFT Research Platform
items.summary: How I architected QuantAlpha Lab, a distributed research platform that bridges the gap between Python data science and Go backend engineering.

items.title: gRPC Service Mesh in Go: Designing the Aegis Auth Platform
items.summary: A walkthrough of Aegis — a modular auth platform built on gRPC inter-service communication, a GraphQL gateway, Kafka audit logging, and full OpenTelemetry trace propagation.

items.title: ADR: Firestore vs PostgreSQL for Event Sourcing in Core Banking
items.summary: An Architecture Decision Record detailing why Firestore was chosen over PostgreSQL as the primary EventStore for the Event-Driven Core Banking platform.

items.title: ADR: Choosing a GraphQL Gateway Over REST for Aegis
items.summary: An Architecture Decision Record detailing why Aegis uses a GraphQL API Gateway to aggregate internal gRPC microservices instead of a traditional REST API.

items.title: Sub-300ms Store Discovery: Designing Geo-Search with Algolia
items.summary: How we leveraged Algolia to build a blazing fast, geo-aware store discovery engine for SeensioGO and Jujuja, achieving 150-300ms latency.

items.title: Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry and Jaeger
items.summary: A practical guide to instrumenting Go microservices with OpenTelemetry: from SDK setup to trace context propagation, sampling strategies, and reading Jaeger flame graphs.

items.title: Event Sourcing vs CRUD: When to Choose Each
items.summary: A decision framework for choosing between Event Sourcing and traditional CRUD, based on building both a CRUD loyalty API and a full event-sourced core banking system.

items.title: Order Book Imbalance (OBI) as a Signal for Short-Term Price Prediction
items.summary: Research notes on extracting Order Book Imbalance (OBI) features from Level-3 market data (VN30F2112) to train rolling-window ML classifiers for High-Frequency Trading.

items.title: Interactive Event Sourcing Replay
items.summary: An interactive visualization of how application state is derived from an immutable, append-only event log.

items.title: Redis Streams vs BullMQ: Choosing Your Job Queue
items.summary: A practical comparison of Redis Streams and BullMQ based on using both in production — covering delivery semantics, consumer group models, and failure handling patterns.

items.title: Interactive Saga State Machine Visualizer
items.summary: An interactive visualization of the Saga distributed transaction pattern, demonstrating automated compensating rollbacks.

items.title: Designing a Multi-Service Auth Platform: The Aegis Architecture
items.summary: A deep dive into Aegis, a high-performance authorization platform using gRPC microservices, a GraphQL gateway, Kafka audit logging, and OpenTelemetry.

items.title: Designing a Real-Time Fraud Detection Engine with Velocity Rules
items.summary: How I built a real-time fraud detection engine using Event Sourcing, CQRS, and velocity rules to automatically freeze malicious accounts in a core banking system.

items.title: Implementing the Saga Pattern for Distributed Money Transfers
items.summary: How I designed a Saga orchestrator pattern for two-phase distributed transfers between account aggregates, with automatic compensation and dead-letter recovery.

items.title: Field Note: Go vs TypeScript for Backend Services
items.summary: A working engineer's honest comparison of Go and TypeScript for backend services, based on using both in production — and a framework for choosing between them.

items.title: Benchmark: Event Replay in PostgreSQL vs Firestore
items.summary: An interactive benchmark comparing the time it takes to replay tens of thousands of immutable events into a Read Projection.

items.title: Benchmark: Go vs TypeScript Concurrency
items.summary: An interactive benchmark visualizing memory footprint and execution time for handling tens of thousands of concurrent network-bound tasks.

items.title: Event-Driven Core Banking System
items.summary: A core banking ledger demonstrating Event Sourcing, CQRS, and distributed Saga transfers.

items.title: Atomic Financial Transactions in a NoSQL World: Building the J-Point Loyalty Engine
items.summary: Implementing virtual currency transactions on Firestore with <1% consistency errors, covering atomic operation design and edge case handling.

items.title: Designing a Burst-Traffic Async Job Pipeline: The Jujuja Quest System
items.summary: How we redesigned daily quest processing from synchronous handlers to a queue-driven worker pool that handles 1,500 concurrent users during campaign windows.
